children: Stock index futures were lower on Thursday as investors weighed escalating geopolitical risks and corporate earnings.
Here are the five news items investors should watch:
Meta Platforms approves new Class C shares:
Meta
shareholders holding most voting

approved a new Class C common stock and changes to its 2025 Equity Incentive Plan. The changes are expected to take effect Jan. 19, 2027, with the shares trading on Nasdaq. The company expects to use the stock to fund AI investments, employee compensation, and acquisitions without changing existing voting power.
DOE releases heating oil reserves:
The U.S. Department of Energy authorized an exchange of up to 315 million barrels of heating oil from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve to ease rising fuel costs ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm
. Heating oil prices in Maine have climbed about 80% from a year ago, increasing pressure on household energy budgets across New England.
Anthropic prepares potential IPO filing:
Anthropic
could publicly file its S-1 registration statement as early as Friday, Oct. 23, Yahoo Finance

, citing three people familiar with the plans. The filing would provide investors with more detail on the Claude developer’s revenue growth, customer concentration, computing expenses, and AI-related risks. The company confidentially submitted a draft registration statement to the SEC in June.
AI uncovers critical PHP vulnerabilities:
Developers of PHP released urgent security fixes Wednesday after AI-assisted efforts uncovered critical vulnerabilities that had gone undetected for years. Alphabet
, OpenAI
, and Amazon

have participated in efforts to identify the flaws and help protect affected systems. The developers urged users to update immediately, highlighting growing demand for cybersecurity tools and software maintenance.
European car registrations gain as EVs surge:

New passenger car registrations in the European Union rose 5.7% in the first nine months of 2026, while battery-electric vehicle registrations climbed about 48% year over year to 1.93 million. Fully electric vehicles accounted for 22.7% of new registrations, up from 16.1% a year earlier. September registrations increased 9.3%, with all four major markets posting growth.
